item.title: THIS SATURDAY SEPT. 19th | Pisgah Brewing Presents: Son Volt with Shannon McNally — Thu Sep 17 — Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain
item.description:
Saturday, September 19, 2026 7:30 PM | Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Outdoor Stage | $36.15 adv. Event Details and Tickets
After spearheading the alt-country movement with Uncle Tupelo, Jay Farrar pursued his vision with Son Volt, who recorded three landmark albums in the ’90s before the groundbreaking artist put the band on extended hiatus and cut three solo LPs. Missing the free exchange of ideas and the surprises that inevitably occur when a group of simpatico musicians lock together, Farrar assembled a new lineup of Son Volt in 2004 and has since released nine albums. The latest album, Sound Signal Serenades, was released as a special 2026 Record Store Day limited edition LP. Jay Farrar’s work often seeks out the ghosts of America’s discordant or forgotten past, converses at length with them, and writes songs that stake a claim to a better future.

item.description:
Saturday, September 19th at 9:00 PM ET | $10.00 tickets, $12.00 at the door Event Details and Tickets Humble is a brand new trio playing funky roots music with songs that run deep like the rivers flowing through the band’s native West Virginia. Drummer Brian Gorby and guitarist Matt Heusel met as members of Humble Sacrifice before forming the Trainjumpers with bassist Scotty Harkness before the idea of a trio was born. Gorby also spent time adding potent rhythms to the Hackensaw Boys before joining Cabinet.
“With Humble, three is all you need to get down to the essence of songs and music.” — Brian Gorby
The band has shared stages with a variety of performers from G-Love to Corey Harris to Les Claypool and Dark Star Orchestra. With Gorby at the root of the band’s sound, funky rhythm is the key, with Heusel and Harkness’ soulful playing added in. The sum is greater than its parts in this musical brotherhood.

item.title: 9:15 Contemplative Service — Sun Sep 20, 9:15 AM — *1 Sanctuary
item.description:
At 9:15 AM, we have a 40-45 minute Contemplative Service. This service invites participants into a reflective, more meditative space, and includes silence, beautiful recorded music and videos, and opportunities for sharing. It also features the sermon and theme which will be the focus in the second service at 11:15 AM. This service is not livestreamed., and it include childcare but not a full religious education program. This service will be particularly good if you need quiet in order to hear well or focus, would prefer a little more space around you, or seek a more contemplative communal experience. Between services, at 10 am we will have coffee hour and special programs. Whether you come to the early service or the later service, we encourage you to consider arriving at 10 am for coffee, conversation, and special programs including conversations with the Board, or Minister & lay-led justice or adult education offerings.
Contact: Rev. Audette Email: revaudette@uuasheville.org

Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS) Few places make a better backdrop for an AYPROS Pub Club than a brewery overlooking the French Broad River. Join AYPROS on **Tuesday, September 22** for our September Pub Club at **New Belgium Brewing**, where we’ll spend the evening at their riverside Asheville brewery and Liquid Center on Craven Street. New Belgium has been part of Asheville’s beer scene for a decade, but the setting alone makes it worth another visit. The 18-acre brewery sits along the French Broad River, with a 6,000-square-foot riverside taproom, plenty of indoor and outdoor space, and furniture and design elements created from repurposed materials and work by local artists. In other words, it is pretty much built for Pub Club.
